intervention_label: Rank-1 shared workup: MGMT promoter methylation (pyrosequencing/MSP), MTAP IHC central confirmation, EGFR amplification + EGFRvIII status, comprehensive tumor NGS (TERT/+7-10/BRAF/NTRK/MMR/MSI/TMB), RB1 functional IHC, p16 IHC corroboration
expected_benefit: Locks every downstream decision before the front-line commit is finalized. MGMT methylation dictates expected benefit from temozolomide and assigns Arm A vs Arm B at NCT07485049 (Stupp HR_OS 0.63 concentrates in methylated tumors per Hegi 2005; unmethylated mOS 12.7 vs 11.8 mo with no significant separation). MTAP IHC by the SP347-class clone is the central confirmation required by AMG 193's MTAPESTRY-101 protocol after 4 of 6 patients enrolled on local CDKN2A-only calls had intact MTAP on central IHC and progressed; the same standard carries to BGB-58067 / MountainTAP-5. EGFR + EGFRvIII is the gate for E-SYNC, CARv3-TEAM-E, and the Penn dual-CAR family. Comprehensive NGS clears or opens dabrafenib + trametinib (BRAF V600E, ROAR ORR 33%), larotrectinib (NTRK), and tumor-agnostic pembrolizumab (MSI-H / TMB-H). RB1 IHC confirms intact RB pathway downstream of CDK4/6 for any abemaciclib conversation at recurrence.
key_risks: No procedural risk — all assays run on archival FFPE from the subtotal-resection block plus a peripheral blood draw for the parallel germline panel. Failure mode is the block itself: intratumoral hemorrhage at presentation may have compromised tumor cellularity in parts of the resection, so pathology should pull the most tumor-rich block and confirm cellularity before sending out the IHC bundle.
Decision risk if MGMT pyrosequencing returns equivocal at the 8-10% cutoff: pair with methylation-array as an orthogonal call (the DKFZ classifier delivers an MGMT readout from the same EPIC array).

Turnaround risk against the RT-start clock: MGMT pyrosequencing 7-10 business days, MTAP + p16 + RB IHC 5-7 business days, EGFR FISH + EGFRvIII RT-PCR 1-2 weeks, comprehensive NGS 2-4 weeks. Order everything in parallel the day after the post-op MRI; do not serialize.
preference_alignment: Trial preference: satisfied (the workup gates every trial slot — BGB-58067 NCT07485049, MountainTAP-5 NCT07492680, GBM AGILE NCT03970447, E-SYNC NCT06186401, CARv3-TEAM-E NCT05660369, SURVIVE NCT05163080). Efficacy lean 0.7: satisfied (gates the MTAP-axis targeted therapy and the MGMT-stratified backbone choice). Modality constraints: none triggered (assays only). Hemorrhage annotation: respected — no contrast or intervention involved.
guideline_status: NCCN CNS v2.2026 mandates MGMT methylation testing on every newly diagnosed IDH-WT GBM; EANO 2021 and ASTRO 2022 concur. Comprehensive NGS with the BRAF V600E, NTRK, and MMR / MSI axes is on the NCCN molecular workup recommendation. MTAP IHC central confirmation is a trial-protocol gate rather than a guideline-level test but is hard-required by every MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor program.
rationale_summary: Every persona endorsed the workup without dissent — the only honest version of the 1L conversation depends on what these tests return. MGMT is the dominant front-line effect modifier (Stupp benefit concentrates in methylated tumors; CeTeG only opens at all in methylated). MTAP IHC is the central-confirmation gate that every MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor protocol now requires after the MTAPESTRY-101 false-positive episode. EGFR / EGFRvIII opens or forecloses the cellular-therapy menu. Comprehensive NGS clears the tumor-agnostic rare actionable lesions at a marginal cost. RB1 + p16 IHC locks the CDK4/6 pathway integrity that the recurrence-time abemaciclib conversation depends on. The entire bundle runs on the existing resection block plus a single blood draw, in parallel, with no procedural risk and turnaround compatible with the standard RT-start window.
open_questions: If MGMT pyrosequencing sits near the 8-10% cutoff, the DKFZ methylation classifier from the same EPIC array gives an orthogonal call that resolves borderline cases (Capper 2018; cIMPACT-NOW Update 9, 2025).

If MTAP IHC returns intact despite the NGS-level loss call, BGB-58067 and MountainTAP-5 enrollment foreclose and the rank-3 row falls off entirely (this is exactly the MTAPESTRY-101 false-positive scenario).

If EGFRvIII returns positive AND MGMT returns unmethylated, the E-SYNC Cohort 1 newly diagnosed front-line cellular-therapy slot opens — but the conservative-issued veto on front-line CAR-T stands unless the screening team can document a hemorrhage-aware re-bleed surveillance plan; see rank 6.

If germline CDKN2A or Lynch panel returns positive on the parallel hereditary-cancer panel, cascade testing of first-degree relatives is triggered and surveillance recommendations for the patient herself shift; this is not therapy-gating but is family-impact gating.
likelihood_of_effect: Diagnostic certainty. Gates the rank-3 MTAP-axis trial enrollment, the rank-4 CeTeG conditional, the rank-6 cellular-therapy pre-position, and every tumor-agnostic conditional rec.
toxicity_burden: Low (none — diagnostic assays on archival FFPE + peripheral blood)

counter_productive_moa.description: Workup row; no therapeutic mechanism to evaluate.

overall: **Six parallel assays on one block of tissue resolve every load-bearing front-line and recurrence-time decision in this case; the RT-start clock argues for sending them all out together this week.**

intervention_label: Stupp regimen + TTFields: RT 60 Gy/30 fx + concurrent TMZ 75 mg/m^2/day × 6 weeks, then 6 cycles adjuvant TMZ 150-200 mg/m^2 d1-5 q28d, with Optune Gio (200 kHz) added from adjuvant cycle 1 at ≥18 hr/day
expected_benefit: Stupp HR_OS 0.63 (95% CI 0.52-0.75, p<0.001), mOS 14.6 vs 12.1 mo, 2-yr OS 26.5% vs 10.4% (EORTC 26981; n=573, RoB2:Low); 5-year update HR 0.6 (0.5-0.7), 5-yr OS 9.8% vs 1.9% (Stupp 2009; replication). TTFields layered on maintenance TMZ: HR_OS 0.63 (95% CI 0.53-0.76, p<0.001), mOS 20.9 vs 16.0 mo, 5-yr OS 13% vs 5% (EF-14; n=695, open-label).
key_risks: Concurrent-phase G≥3 hematologic AE 7%; adjuvant-phase 14% (lymphopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia dominate). At age 66, expect dose modification in roughly a quarter of patients. Weekly CBC during concurrent phase and the first two adjuvant cycles is on-label monitoring.
PJP prophylaxis during concurrent phase is non-negotiable given TMZ-induced lymphopenia; standard mitigation.
TTFields scalp dermatitis 52% any grade, 2% G≥3 — managed by array rotation and topical steroids per the published algorithm. Non-overlapping with TMZ hematotox.
≥18 hr/day Optune wear-time is the binding adherence variable; sub-18-hour wear roughly halves the EF-14 OS benefit per the per-protocol analyses. Counsel the patient honestly before commit.
preference_alignment: User explicitly asked for SoC to be surfaced (free-text framing). Efficacy lean 0.7: satisfied (the only newly diagnosed regimen with replicated phase 3 OS evidence in this population). No toxicity vetoes. Modality (RT + oral TMZ + scalp device) compatible with all stated preferences. Hemorrhage annotation: respected (TMZ + TTFields carries no bleed signal).
guideline_status: NCCN CNS Cancers v2.2026 category 1 (preferred) for newly diagnosed IDH-WT GBM in age <70 KPS ≥70; TTFields category 1 in combination with maintenance TMZ. EANO 2021 and ESMO 2014/2021 concur. Patient (66, ECOG 1) sits inside the EORTC 26981 / EF-14 inclusion population.
rationale_summary: Universal endorsement across all five seats. Stupp is the only newly diagnosed regimen with RoB2:Low phase 3 OS evidence replicated at 5 years; EF-14 adds a second HR 0.63 on top of TMZ. Even the advocate and risktaker — who ranked the MTAP-axis trial higher in their own lists — kept the Stupp backbone explicitly inside the trial design (NCT07485049 Arm A = drug + RT; Arm B = drug + RT + TMZ), so this row is the spine every other rank either layers on or substitutes against. The conservative and critic seats explicitly rejected substituting any phase 1 monotherapy for Stupp, citing CheckMate-498 (HR_OS 1.31 worse than Stupp in unmethylated MGMT, p=0.0037, n=560) as the published cautionary precedent. TTFields is bundled here rather than ranked separately because the EF-14 benefit only realizes on top of TMZ.
open_questions: MGMT methylation result modulates the magnitude of TMZ benefit (Hegi 2005: methylated mOS 21.7 vs 15.3, p<0.001; unmethylated 12.7 vs 11.8, NS). The regimen recommendation does not flip on the methylation result, but the candor of the patient conversation does.

If performance status declines between resection and RT planning, Perry / CCTG CE.6 hypofractionated RT 40 Gy/15 fx + concurrent and adjuvant TMZ is the evidence-grade fallback (NCCN category 1 for age ≥65; HR_OS 0.67 95% CI 0.56-0.80, n=562, Perry 2017).
Optune prior auth: start the Novocure nCompass submission (1-855-281-9301) the same week as RT planning; commercial coverage varies and the device ships only after prior auth clears.
likelihood_of_effect: High — Stupp HR_OS 0.63 (95% CI 0.52-0.75, replicated 5-yr) + EF-14 HR_OS 0.63 (95% CI 0.53-0.76) layered on TMZ; the 20.9-mo median is the threshold every other rank is measured against.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (G≥3 hematologic 14% adjuvant-phase, lymphopenia under TMZ requiring PJP prophylaxis, scalp dermatitis 52% any grade / 2% G≥3 under arrays)

counter_productive_moa.description: TMZ-induced hypermutation at recurrence can paradoxically open MMR-deficient ICI eligibility — a delayed pro-mechanism effect rather than a true counter-productive one.

overall: **The OS-anchored standard the entire ranking is built around; every other rank either layers on this backbone or is measured against it.**

intervention_label: BGB-58067 (brain-penetrant MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor) on the Sanai phase 0/2 NCT07485049 at Ivy Brain Tumor Center, Phoenix — Arm A (unmethylated MGMT + RT) or Arm B (methylated MGMT + RT + TMZ); layered on the Stupp backbone, not substituting for it
expected_benefit: Mechanism-matched targeted therapy at the patient's lead actionable feature (MTAP/CDKN2A 9p21 co-deletion). Direct human-GBM efficacy data on BGB-58067 itself is not yet published; the class proxy is anvumetostat (AMG 193) MTAPESTRY-101 (Rodon AnnOnc 2024 / Cancer Discovery 2025, n=80) at ORR 11% in heavily pre-treated all-comer MTAP-null tumors with G≥3 TRAE 13.8% and treatment discontinuation 2.5% — the cleanest PRMT5 class safety on record, with 56% median plasma SDMA reduction at C2D1 confirming target engagement. The structural value of NCT07485049 is the SDMA pharmacodynamic readout on phase 0 re-resection tissue, which forces a target-engagement decision before phase 2 commits dose, and the MGMT-stratified arm design.
key_risks: No published peer-reviewed phase 1 safety or efficacy on BGB-58067 specifically; CSF exposure data for the molecule has not been disclosed. Class CNS track record is TNG908 terminated November 2024 (0/23 GBM ORR, CSF n=3 confirming inadequate brain exposure) and anvumetostat discontinued by Amgen April 30, 2026 across four phase 1b/2 trials. BGB-58067 was engineered with explicit CNS-exposure modeling against the TNG908 failure mode but the human data closing that loop is not yet public.

Phase 0 component requires a second resection biopsy for the SDMA / H-score readout. Subtotal-resection block tumor cellularity needs pathology confirmation; the intratumoral hemorrhage at presentation may have compromised that, and feasibility of repeat craniotomy at 66 with ECOG 1 is the screening conversation.

Single US site (Ivy Brain Tumor Center / St Joseph's Hospital, Phoenix). Geographic move plus travel and lodging cost is real; Ivy has limited assistance funds — the Phase 0 Navigator (602-406-8605) can confirm what is available.

Eligibility hard-gated on central MTAP IHC by the SP347-class clone (the same standard MTAPESTRY-101 required after the four-of-six false-positive episode) and on the MGMT methylation result for arm assignment.
preference_alignment: Trial preference: fully satisfied (this is the single best mechanism-matched currently-recruiting trial in the dossier). Efficacy lean 0.7: satisfied via targeted-therapy upside. No toxicity vetoes triggered. Free-text 'surface all possible options' explicitly named the PRMT5 class by molecule — the user wrote the preference file with this trial in mind. Hemorrhage annotation: respected (no antiangiogenic exposure; the only feasibility concern is the phase 0 re-resection itself).
guideline_status: Not in any guideline. NCCN CNS v2.2026 names clinical trial enrollment as a top-of-pathway recommendation across every GBM treatment pathway, and the trial design layers BGB-58067 on the category-1 Stupp backbone rather than substituting for it — that framing carries the rec into the guideline-aligned slot the consensusite seat reads as enrollment-on-top-of-SoC. MTAP loss is not yet a guideline-endorsed treatment-decision variable in any NCCN / ESMO / EANO version.
rationale_summary: All five seats listed BGB-58067, but the ranking conversation split the board. The advocate and risktaker put it at rank 1; the conservative ranked it 3, the consensusite 3, and the critic 5 — all citing the same load-bearing concern, which is the absence of peer-reviewed BGB-58067 safety on the molecule itself plus the class's CNS failure record (TNG908 terminated; anvumetostat discontinued). The conservative dissent on the advocate's rank-1 placement was explicit on toxicity grounds and is contingent — the conservative noted it lifts to qualified once Sanai publishes the phase 0 PD / safety readout. The synthesis ranks it 3 — below the OS-anchored Stupp + TTFields spine but above the more-conditional CeTeG and tumor-agnostic options — because the trial preserves the Stupp backbone inside its arm design, the biomarker fit is exact, the brain-penetrant chemistry is the engineered answer to the proximate TNG908 failure mode, and the user's preference file named the PRMT5 class by molecule. The dissent is on rank order, not on inclusion. Honest framing to the patient: open phase 0/2 slot at a high-volume center with no efficacy data yet on the molecule.
open_questions: Whether Sanai will publish the phase 0 BGB-58067 PD / safety readout before the patient's screening conversation — if so, the conservative and critic dissents lift from this row.
Whether the subtotal-resection block has enough tumor cellularity for the SDMA / H-score readout, or whether a second-look operation would be the path to the phase 0 slot.
Whether the patient and family can absorb the Phoenix travel cost; ask the Ivy Phase 0 Navigator (602-406-8605) about current assistance-fund availability.

Whether the MountainTAP-5 (NCT07492680, BMS-986504 + TMZ + RT cohort, opens July 2026) becomes a closer-to-home parallel-track option once it activates — the BMS sponsor is multi-site by design and the trial explicitly lists newly diagnosed GBM.
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate uncertainty — mechanism-matched at MTAP/CDKN2A with brain-penetrant chemistry but no published BGB-58067 efficacy on the molecule itself; class proxy ORR ~11% in pre-treated all-comer MTAP-null tumors (anvumetostat MTAPESTRY-101).
toxicity_burden: Low (class proxy: G≥3 TRAE 13.8%, discontinuation 2.5%, no treatment-related deaths in anvumetostat MTAPESTRY-101; BGB-58067 CNS-specific tox unpublished)

counter_productive_moa.description: Inadequate CNS exposure was the proximate failure mode of TNG908 — design rationale addresses it but human CSF PK on BGB-58067 itself is not yet public.

overall: **The cleanest mechanistic match in the dossier for this patient's 9p21 co-deletion; biomarker fit is exact and the trial preserves the Stupp backbone, but the molecule has no published human efficacy and the class's CNS record is two failures.**

intervention_label: CeTeG / NOA-09: lomustine (CCNU) 100 mg/m^2 day 1 + TMZ 100-200 mg/m^2 days 2-6 every 6 weeks × 6 cycles, with concurrent RT 60 Gy — conditional on MGMT promoter methylated AND adequate baseline marrow reserve
expected_benefit: In MGMT-methylated newly diagnosed GBM, mOS 48.1 vs 31.4 mo, HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.35-1.03, one-sided p=0.049 per-protocol) — a 16.7-month median OS gain over standard Stupp (Herrlinger 2019 Lancet; n=141, RoB2:Some, open-label). The largest published front-line OS signal in the MGMT-methylated stratum.
key_risks: G≥3 hematologic AE 41% (CeTeG arm) vs 13% (TMZ-alone), driven by lymphopenia 27%, thrombocytopenia 16%, neutropenia 13%. At age 66, the cumulative CCNU myelosuppression bites — many patients need dose reduction by cycle 3, and platelet recovery becomes dose-rate-limiting by cycles 4-6.

Open-label phase 3 (RoB2:Some leaning Serious), n=141, primary analyzed per-protocol with one-sided p=0.049 and a 95% CI of 0.35-1.03 that crosses 1.0 on the upper bound. The 48-mo median OS is not a number to quote without the CI caveat.
No independent replication. The OS signal is real but the precision is not Stupp-grade.
Set CBC weekly during the first two cycles, then per protocol; pre-set platelet and ANC thresholds and the CCNU dose-reduction algorithm at consent.
preference_alignment: Efficacy lean 0.7: highly satisfied conditional on methylated status (largest published OS gain in 1L GBM). No toxicity vetoes. SoC-aligned (NCCN cat 2A). User explicitly asked for the full menu — this is the conditional methylated-MGMT play.
guideline_status: NCCN CNS v2.2026 category 2A for newly diagnosed MGMT-methylated GBM with KPS ≥70; EANO 2021 names it as an option in the same population with the explicit hematologic-toxicity caveat. The 2A designation reflects uniform expert consensus on lower-level evidence — collective calibration of the same Herrlinger 2019 paper.
rationale_summary: Four seats endorsed CeTeG explicitly (the risktaker did not pick it but did not contest it; treated as not-listed-not-dissenting). The conservative and critic seats independently flagged the same evidence-quality concerns — open-label, n=141, per-protocol primary, 95% CI crossing 1.0 — and the consensusite read the NCCN 2A designation as the collective calibration of those concerns. There is no veto and no rank-order dissent on this row; the conditional framing (methylated-only, marrow-reserve-adequate) is what every persona converged on. If MGMT returns unmethylated, this rank falls off entirely and the row's slot reverts to rank-3 enrollment or rank-2 Stupp alone.
open_questions: MGMT pyrosequencing result is the gate. Methylated and adequate marrow (ANC ≥1500, platelets ≥100k): viable. Unmethylated: this row drops off, no rationale.
Functional reserve at age 66: CGA or modified G8 before committing to six cycles of doublet alkylator is the conservative-flagged due diligence.

If the patient elects BGB-58067 NCT07485049 Arm B (methylated MGMT + RT + TMZ), CeTeG and the trial cannot be run concurrently — the trial protocol does not include CCNU in the backbone, and committing to CeTeG outside the trial forecloses the BGB-58067 slot in Arm B.
likelihood_of_effect: High in MGMT-methylated subset — Herrlinger 2019 HR_OS 0.60 (95% CI 0.35-1.03), mOS 48.1 vs 31.4 mo; CI precision is modest at n=141 and unreplicated.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (G≥3 hematologic 41%: lymphopenia 27%, thrombocytopenia 16%, neutropenia 13%; no treatment-related deaths in CeTeG arm)

counter_productive_moa.description: Cumulative CCNU myelosuppression can foreclose later cytotoxic combinations at recurrence (lomustine + bevacizumab) — a sequencing rather than a counter-productive concern.

overall: **The largest published front-line OS signal in MGMT-methylated GBM, conditional on a result the workup row will return; toxicity at age 66 is the binding constraint and the CI is wider than the headline number suggests.**
scenario_label: If MGMT pyrosequencing returns methylated at the 8-10% cutoff

intervention_label: GBM AGILE adaptive platform (NCT03970447) — Bayesian-randomized multi-site backbone alternative; current arms AZD1390 + RT (newly diagnosed only), tinostamustine, ADI-PEG 20, troriluzole, VT1021
expected_benefit: Multi-site Bayesian adaptive platform with randomized control against current SoC and OS as primary endpoint. No MTAP-matched arm currently active, so this is the second-best randomized trial route for this patient's biology; AZD1390 (ATM kinase inhibitor + RT) and tinostamustine (HDAC + alkylator) are the most likely newly-diagnosed assignments by molecular subgroup.
key_risks: No current AGILE arm targets MTAP or CDKN2A. Randomization could land the patient on the standard-Stupp control arm — a defensible outcome but not the molecularly targeted axis the user asked for.
Single screening assigns to arm; the patient does not pick. Bayesian randomization weights toward the better-performing arms over time but the individual assignment is opaque.
Multi-site infrastructure addresses the single-site fragility of NCT07485049 — this is the right fallback if Phoenix is geographically infeasible or the BGB-58067 slot is taken.
preference_alignment: Trial preference: satisfied (well-designed randomized platform; every major guideline endorses enrollment). Efficacy lean 0.7: partially satisfied — the platform construct is strong but the current arm list does not hit MTAP. Modality: no constraints triggered.
guideline_status: NCCN CNS v2.2026 trial-enrollment language and EANO 2021 / ESMO 2021 platform-trial endorsement carry this; not in any disease-specific guideline as a discrete arm.
rationale_summary: The advocate and consensusite seats picked GBM AGILE explicitly as the randomized-multi-site fallback to BGB-58067; the conservative, critic, and risktaker did not pick it but did not contest it. The honest framing is that AGILE is structurally the strongest randomized-trial slot the patient could enter, and the Bayesian adaptive design plus randomized control against current SoC is what every major guideline endorses. The mechanism axis is the weak spot — none of the active arms maps to MTAP or CDKN2A — so this row is positioned below the mechanism-matched BGB-58067 even though it has the stronger trial-design profile.
open_questions: Whether the patient prefers a randomized-platform slot with multi-site infrastructure (lower geographic burden, higher trial-quality framework) or a mechanism-matched single-arm phase 0/2 (lower randomization risk, higher biological fit) — both are guideline-aligned trial-enrollment paths.

GBM AGILE screening is fast; if the BGB-58067 Phoenix slot is taken or Phoenix is infeasible, enrollment here can proceed in days rather than weeks. Contact GCAR at 310-598-3199 or patientinfo@gcaresearch.org.
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate — Bayesian randomization against SoC; current arms (AZD1390+RT, tinostamustine, ADI-PEG 20) are not MTAP-matched, so mechanism-axis upside is lower than BGB-58067.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (varies by arm assignment; AZD1390+RT carries CNS toxicity and lymphopenia signal, tinostamustine carries hematologic AE typical of alkylators)

counter_productive_moa.description: Arm randomization can land the patient on a non-mechanism-matched investigational agent — efficiency cost rather than counter-productive mechanism.

overall: **The strongest multi-site randomized-platform alternative when the Phoenix slot is infeasible; mechanism axis is weaker than BGB-58067 because no current arm targets MTAP.**

intervention_label: SurVaxM (survivin peptide vaccine SVN53-67/M57-KLH) + GM-CSF on the SURVIVE phase 2b NCT05163080, layered on adjuvant TMZ
expected_benefit: Single-arm phase 2a (Ahluwalia 2023 JCO, n=63, informal:med RoB): PFS6 95.2%, mPFS 11.4 mo, mOS 25.9 mo, 2-yr OS 51%, 3-yr OS 41% — encouraging vs the historical ~16-mo control but explicitly non-randomized. SURVIVE (NCT05163080) is the randomized phase 2b validation gate. The standout property is safety: injection-site reactions and low-grade flu-like symptoms dominate; zero SurVaxM-attributable G≥3 SAEs in the published n=63.
key_risks: Single-arm phase 2a with non-contemporaneous historical control — magnitude of OS signal is not yet confirmed. SURVIVE is the randomized phase 2b answer.
SURVIVE status changed to active not recruiting as of February 2024 verification — re-screen for site reopenings by calling Roswell Park at 1-800-ROSWELL (1-800-767-9355).
If patient also enrolls in BGB-58067 (rank 3), check protocol-level vaccine co-administration restrictions; many trials exclude concurrent investigational immunotherapy.
Post-Stupp slot only — vaccination starts after concurrent RT + TMZ completion, requires KPS ≥70 and dexamethasone ≤4 mg/day, and no prior immunotherapy or Optune (incompatible with rank 2 TTFields).
preference_alignment: Trial preference: satisfied. Efficacy lean 0.7: partially satisfied (single-arm phase 2a signal; randomized confirmation pending). No toxicity vetoes. Compatible with hemorrhage annotation (peptide vaccine carries no bleed signal). Important conflict with rank 2: the SURVIVE protocol excludes Optune use, so the patient cannot run TTFields and SurVaxM concurrently.
rationale_summary: Only the conservative seat picked SurVaxM explicitly (at rank 5). The pick is defensible on safety alone — the toxicity floor here is the lowest of any add-on the dossier surfaces, and the phase 2a OS signal is encouraging. No persona dissented; the rec sits at rank 6 because the evidence base is single-arm phase 2a and the randomized phase 2b SURVIVE has not yet read out. The Optune-incompatibility is the load-bearing practical conflict: the patient cannot run rank 2 TTFields and SurVaxM together, so the choice is between the EF-14-anchored 5-yr OS lift (rank 2) and the single-arm vaccine-add-on signal (this row).
open_questions: Whether SURVIVE has reopened any US site for new enrollment — call Roswell Park (1-800-767-9355) before committing time to screening.

Whether the patient elects TTFields (rank 2) or SurVaxM (this row); the SURVIVE protocol forecloses concurrent Optune. The conservative-recommended answer in the absence of fresh data is rank 2 TTFields with its replicated phase 3 OS evidence over the unreplicated single-arm signal here.
If the trial is permanently closed to new enrollment, MimiVax expanded access exists but is more expensive than trial enrollment; pursue NCT05163080 first.
likelihood_of_effect: Low-to-moderate — Ahluwalia 2023 single-arm n=63 reported PFS6 95.2%, mOS 25.9 mo against ~16-mo historical control; SURVIVE phase 2b is the randomized validation gate.
toxicity_burden: Low (injection-site reactions, low-grade flu-like symptoms; zero SurVaxM-attributable G≥3 SAEs in n=63)

counter_productive_moa.description: Vaccine adjuvant immune activation has no established counter-productive mechanism in GBM; the main concern is Optune incompatibility (foregoing EF-14-anchored OS) rather than a mechanism-level risk.

overall: **The lowest-toxicity add-on in the dossier with a real but unreplicated single-arm signal; forces a binary choice against TTFields because SURVIVE excludes concurrent Optune.**

intervention_label: Tumor-agnostic conditional plays unlocked by the rank-1 NGS panel: dabrafenib + trametinib for BRAF V600E (ROAR HGG cohort); larotrectinib or entrectinib for NTRK fusion-positive; pembrolizumab for MSI-H / dMMR or TMB-H — all recurrence-only and biomarker-conditional
expected_benefit: Dabrafenib + trametinib in BRAF V600E HGG (ROAR, Wen 2022 Lancet Oncol, n=45): ORR 33% (95% CI 20-49), mDoR 13.6 mo, 12-mo OS 41%. Larotrectinib in TRK-fusion solid tumors (Drilon 2018 NEJM, n=55): ORR 75-80% with CNS responses confirmed in Doz 2022. Pembrolizumab in TMB-H ≥10 mut/Mb (Marabelle 2020 / KEYNOTE-158, n=102): ORR 29% (95% CI 21-39). Each conditional gate has low prior probability in adult IDH-WT GBM (BRAF V600E ~1-2%, NTRK <1%, primary MMR-D / MSI-H uncommon) but the upside on a positive hit is large enough to reframe the second-line decision tree.
key_risks: Low prior probability across all three biomarkers — these are recurrence-pre-positions, not active 1L recommendations.
DNA-only NGS panels miss NTRK intron-deep breakpoints in CNS tumors; insist on RNA-based fusion testing (Tempus xR or Caris WTS) as part of the rank-1 NGS bundle.

Front-line ICI in unselected GBM is explicitly NOT guideline-endorsed and is contraindicated by CheckMate-498 (Omuro 2023, n=560, RoB2:Low, HR_OS 1.31 worse than Stupp in MGMT-unmethylated, p=0.0037). These ICI recs sit in the biomarker-gated recurrence branch only.

Class AEs by axis: dabrafenib+trametinib (pyrexia, rash, fatigue; manageable); larotrectinib (transaminitis, dizziness; well-tolerated); pembrolizumab (immune-related AE spectrum; baseline TSH/AM cortisol/LFT).
preference_alignment: Trial preference: satisfied (each conditional axis opens trial enrollment when positive). Efficacy lean 0.7: satisfied conditional on a positive hit. No toxicity vetoes. NGS bundle is being ordered as part of rank-1 workup anyway — marginal cost is zero.
guideline_status: NCCN CNS v2.2026 lists all three on the recurrent/refractory branch when biomarker positive: dabrafenib + trametinib for BRAF V600E (tumor-agnostic label), larotrectinib / entrectinib for NTRK fusion (tumor-agnostic), pembrolizumab for MSI-H / dMMR (tumor-agnostic) or TMB-H ≥10 mut/Mb (tumor-agnostic). Cross-society convergence is real across NCCN, ESMO, ASCO.
rationale_summary: The consensusite picked these explicitly at ranks 6-7-8 of their list; the risktaker bundled them at rank 4 as 'essentially free options' once the NGS panel returns. The conservative and critic did not pick them but did not contest the framing — the comprehensive NGS is part of the workup row everyone endorsed at rank 1, and these are the rare-actionable lesion conditional plays that fall out of it. Honest priors are low; the marginal cost is zero because the NGS bundle is being run anyway; the upside on a positive hit reframes the second-line tree.
open_questions: Order RNA-based fusion testing alongside the standard DNA panel — CNS NTRK breakpoints are often intron-deep.
If MMR / MSI returns abnormal on the tumor side, escalate germline Lynch / CMMRD panel (essential row in target_validation) and trigger cascade testing of first-degree relatives.

Pembrolizumab at recurrence opens only if biomarker-positive; treating-team conversation must acknowledge CheckMate-498 / CheckMate-548 / NRG-BN007 / CheckMate-143 negatives in unselected populations.
likelihood_of_effect: Low prior probability across all three biomarkers in adult IDH-WT GBM (BRAF V600E ~1-2%, NTRK <1%, MMR-D uncommon); ORR conditional on a positive hit is ROAR 33%, larotrectinib 75-80%, pembrolizumab TMB-H 29%.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (class AEs by axis; mostly manageable on outpatient monitoring)

counter_productive_moa.description: Each axis is biomarker-selected; mechanism-level risk only arises if a positive call is acted on without confirmation (e.g. NTRK call without RNA-fusion verification).

overall: **Free conditional options that fall out of the rank-1 NGS bundle at zero marginal cost; low prior probability across all three but the upside on a positive hit reframes the recurrence-time decision tree.**

intervention_label: Navlimetostat (BMS-986504) on the MountainTAP-5 phase 2 NCT07492680 — Cohort 4 explicitly combines BMS-986504 with TMZ + RT for newly diagnosed MTAP-deleted GBM; pin for July 2026 re-screen
expected_benefit: Parallel-track MTAP-axis insurance against BGB-58067 single-site fragility. Same MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor class with explicit GBM cohort and a Stupp-backbone combination arm built into the protocol design. Patient meets MTAP-null gate and ECOG 0-1 fits.
key_risks: Not yet recruiting — planned open July 17, 2026. Cannot act on this in May 2026 except to set the re-screen calendar trigger.

BMS-986504 CSF PK in human GBM is not publicly characterized like BGB-58067; the molecule was originated at Mirati and is the BMS lifecycle-managed successor to anvumetostat, which the closest molecular relative is dead (Amgen discontinued April 30, 2026).
Pipeline-context pick; not first-line enrollment today.
preference_alignment: Trial preference: satisfied as forward-looking. Efficacy lean 0.7: satisfied via mechanism match. Hemorrhage annotation: respected (no antiangiogenic component).
guideline_status: Not in any guideline; phase 2 stage.
rationale_summary: The advocate (rank 8) and risktaker (parallel-track backup) flagged this as the MTAP-axis parallel-track insurance against the BGB-58067 single-site fragility. No persona dissented. The honest framing is calendar logistics: pin July 2026 in the chart, call the BMS Clinical Trials Contact Center (855-907-3286) the week the protocol opens, and have the MTAP IHC central confirmation ready from the rank-1 workup. If BGB-58067 enrollment fails for any reason — slot taken, Phoenix travel infeasible, phase 0 re-resection not viable — MountainTAP-5 becomes the patient-relevant MTAP-axis option once it activates.
open_questions: Whether the Cohort 4 newly-diagnosed-GBM combination arm activates as planned in July 2026 and whether the trial accepts patients post-RT-start versus pre-RT-start.
Whether the BMS protocol's MTAP-confirmation assay matches the SP347-class IHC the rank-1 workup will return; if not, a re-stain at the trial central lab may be needed.
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate — same class as BGB-58067 with explicit GBM + Stupp-backbone cohort; class proxy is anvumetostat MTAPESTRY-101 (ORR 11% in pre-treated all-comer MTAP-null tumors).
toxicity_burden: Low (class proxy: G≥3 TRAE 13.8% in anvumetostat MTAPESTRY-101; BMS-986504 specific tox profile in escalation)

counter_productive_moa.description: Same class-level concern as BGB-58067: human CSF PK on BMS-986504 in GBM is not yet public; CNS exposure is the historical failure mode for the class.

overall: **Parallel-track insurance on the MTAP axis against BGB-58067 single-site fragility; not actionable today, calendar-trigger July 2026 the week MountainTAP-5 opens.**

intervention_label: Abemaciclib (CDK4/6 inhibitor, CNS-penetrant) off-label or on a PRMT5 + CDK4/6 combination protocol at first progression — leveraging the 9p21 co-deletion (CDKN2A loss + MTAP loss) synthetic-lethal logic; gated on RB1 functional confirmation
expected_benefit: Recurrent CDKN2A-deleted / RB-intact GBM monotherapy ceiling is modest: Wen 2024 NCT02981940 (n=42) PFS6 9.7% (95% CI 2.5-22.9), with paired-surgical PK confirming intratumoral concentrations at pharmacologically relevant levels. INSIGhT abemaciclib arm (Wen 2023 CCR, n=73): HR_PFS 0.72 (95% CI 0.49-1.06, one-sided p=0.046), no OS benefit; PFS CI crosses 1.0. The combination case (PRMT5 + CDK4/6 at progression) rests on preclinical convergence: Vilgelm 2019 and the AACR 2025 TNG462 + CDK4/6 data show deeper regression than either agent alone in MTAP-null / CDKN2A-null / RB-intact models.
key_risks: Monotherapy activity in recurrent CDKN2A-loss GBM is modest (PFS6 ~9.7%); the combination case is preclinical with no clinical PRMT5 + CDK4/6i trial in GBM today.

Palbociclib failure (Taal 2018 PMID:30151703, n=22, mPFS 1.2 mo, closed early for futility) is the cautionary precedent — palbociclib is a Pgp substrate and does not get to tumor. Use abemaciclib or ribociclib only.

Off-label off-protocol GBM use faces a payer fight: the NCCN Compendium does NOT currently list GBM as a compendia-supported off-label use, so the medical-exception letter rests on documented CDKN2A loss + intact RB and the published Tien 2019 ribociclib phase 0 + INSIGhT abemaciclib pharmacodynamic data.

Class AEs: diarrhea (characteristic, dose-limiting), neutropenia, fatigue. Manageable at age 66 with appropriate dose modification; start 150 mg BID with close monitoring rather than the on-label 200 mg BID.
Gated on RB1 functional IHC from the rank-1 workup. RB1 loss closes the rationale entirely.
preference_alignment: Trial preference: partially satisfied (the active GBM CDK4/6 protocols — NCT02981940, INSIGhT abemaciclib arm — are closed to accrual). Efficacy lean 0.7: marginally satisfied (PFS without OS in monotherapy; combination thesis is preclinical). No toxicity vetoes. Hemorrhage annotation: respected.
guideline_status: NCCN category 1 for breast-cancer indications; OFF-guideline for GBM. NCCN Compendium does not list GBM as a compendia-supported off-label use.
rationale_summary: The advocate and risktaker both flagged abemaciclib as a recurrence pre-position keyed to the patient's textbook 9p21 co-deletion plus the CDK4/6 + PRMT5 preclinical combination rationale. The critic and consensusite explicitly did NOT rank it: the critic on evidence quality (PFS without OS; modest monotherapy ceiling; Taal 2018 palbociclib failure) and the consensusite on off-guideline status (NCCN Compendium does not list GBM). The synthesis includes it at rank 9 because the mechanistic logic is precisely the patient's biology and the recurrence-time combination conversation deserves to be on the radar, but with explicit acknowledgment that the dissent on evidence-quality and guideline-fit is load-bearing. Status: considered_with_caveats. Not a 1L pick at any rank.
open_questions: Whether a brain-penetrant PRMT5 inhibitor (BGB-58067, TNG456 successor, or BMS-986504) becomes accessible at progression in a way that supports an off-protocol abemaciclib + PRMT5 combination — the treating center's compassionate-use review board is the gate.
Whether the rank-1 RB1 IHC returns intact (rationale stands) or lost (rationale closes).

Whether the payer accepts a medical-exception letter citing CDKN2A loss + intact RB + Tien 2019 + INSIGhT — Lilly Answers (1-800-545-5979) will provide the published off-label medical-information dossier on request.
likelihood_of_effect: Low for monotherapy (PFS6 ~9.7% recurrent CDKN2A-loss GBM, Wen 2024); the combination case (CDK4/6i + PRMT5i) is preclinical and untested in clinic.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (G≥3 diarrhea characteristic of class, neutropenia, fatigue; at age 66 start at 150 mg BID rather than on-label 200 mg BID)

counter_productive_moa.description: Pgp efflux at the BBB blunts the CDK4/6 class in CNS (Taal palbociclib failure); abemaciclib was selected for partial CNS penetration but intratumoral concentrations are modest.

overall: **Recurrence-time pre-position keyed to the patient's exact 9p21 co-deletion biology; monotherapy ceiling is modest and the combination thesis is preclinical, so the rank is honest about the evidence gap.**

intervention_label: CAN-3110 (rQNestin34.5v.2) oncolytic HSV-1 intratumoral injection — recurrence pre-position; order HSV-1 IgG serology now to inform the prior probability of benefit
expected_benefit: Ling 2023 Nature phase 1 in recurrent HGG: single-dose mOS 11.6 mo overall, mOS 14.2 mo in the HSV-1 seropositive subset (~66% of cohort) — roughly 2× the historical recurrent-GBM benchmark. FDA Fast Track and Orphan Drug Designation for recurrent HGG in 2024. No DLTs across the full dose range.
key_risks: Recurrent-disease only; currently active not recruiting at the Dana-Farber lead site. Pre-position only.

Intratumoral injection feasibility depends on residual disease anatomy and any second-look surgical plan; the patient's intratumoral-hemorrhage history is a relative caution because perilesional inflammation from viral lysis overlaps with the bleed mechanism — annotate, do not exclude.
Order HSV-1 IgG serology now: the test costs ~$20, and a seropositive result roughly doubles the prior probability of benefit when the recurrence conversation happens.
preference_alignment: Trial preference: pre-positioned. Efficacy lean 0.7: satisfied via the HSV-1 seropositive subset signal. No toxicity vetoes. Hemorrhage annotation: respected with a relative caution flag.
guideline_status: Not in NCCN; FDA Fast Track 2024 for recurrent HGG.
rationale_summary: Both the advocate and risktaker flagged CAN-3110 as a recurrence pre-position, with the HSV-1 IgG serology as the no-brainer test to order now (cheap, informs prior probability). No dissent. The hemorrhage-history caution is real but not exclusionary; the Ling 2023 cohort included patients with prior tumor bleeding without prohibitive re-bleed rates. The synthesis carries the rec at rank 10 as recurrence-only insurance with the serology recommended this week.
open_questions: HSV-1 IgG serology result (positive doubles the prior probability of benefit per the Ling 2023 seropositive subset).
Whether NCT03152318 reopens to enrollment or pivots to a successor protocol when the patient progresses.
Whether the patient's residual disease anatomy at recurrence supports intratumoral injection; second-look craniotomy candidacy is the gate.
likelihood_of_effect: Low overall, moderate in HSV-1 seropositive subset — Ling 2023 single-dose mOS 11.6 mo overall, 14.2 mo seropositive vs ~9 mo historical recurrent-GBM benchmark.
toxicity_burden: Low (no DLTs across the Ling 2023 dose range; perilesional inflammation is the modal AE)

counter_productive_moa.description: Perilesional inflammation from viral lysis could re-bleed in a pre-bled brain — a hemorrhage-history-specific relative caution rather than a class-level counter-productive mechanism.

overall: **Recurrence-time pre-position with a cheap up-front serology that doubles the prior probability of benefit; hemorrhage history is a relative caution not an exclusion.**

intervention_label: FUS-mediated BBB opening (SonoCloud-9 / SONOBIRD NCT04528680) at first recurrence — pre-position at a US SONOBIRD site (Northwestern/Sonabend, Columbia, MD Anderson)
expected_benefit: Sonabend 2023 Lancet Oncology phase 1 (n=17): 4-6× increased peri-tumoral nab-paclitaxel concentration vs unsonicated brain on the SonoCloud-9 implant, no implant-related deaths, tolerated through 6 cycles. SONOBIRD is the phase 3 (n=560, 40 sites US+EU) with IV carboplatin as the partner drug, randomized vs lomustine or TMZ at first recurrence.
key_risks: Recurrent-only with planned re-resection — not actionable today. Requires surgical candidacy at first progression.
Implant decision must be made AT the re-resection operation, not afterward — pre-position the patient at a SONOBIRD US site early so the conversation can happen at the right moment.
Survival data not yet mature; SONOBIRD readout is the validation gate. The bet here is on the drug-delivery mechanism rather than the OS data.
preference_alignment: Trial preference: pre-positioned. Efficacy lean 0.7: speculative — bet is on delivery enhancement, not on the partner drug's intrinsic activity. No toxicity vetoes.
guideline_status: Not in NCCN; FDA Breakthrough Device Designation 2022 for SonoCloud-9.
rationale_summary: Only the risktaker picked FUS-BBB explicitly. No dissent from other personas. The pre-position value is real: any antibody-class or large-molecule CNS therapy that gets blocked at the BBB becomes accessible behind FUS sonication, which opens off-label combinations at recurrence. Pre-positioning the patient at Northwestern (Sonabend) or another US SONOBIRD site at the first-recurrence resection conversation is the actionable step today.
open_questions: Whether the patient becomes a surgical candidate for re-resection at first recurrence — required for the SonoCloud-9 implant.
Which US SONOBIRD site is geographically closest; call Adam Sonabend's team at Northwestern as the leading published US investigator.
likelihood_of_effect: Low-to-moderate — Sonabend 2023 (n=17) demonstrated 4-6× peri-tumoral drug concentration enhancement; SONOBIRD OS data not yet mature.
toxicity_burden: Low (no implant-related deaths in Sonabend 2023; tolerated through 6 cycles)

counter_productive_moa.description: BBB opening could theoretically increase off-target CNS exposure of partner cytotoxics, but the Sonabend cohort showed no implant-related deaths or severe CNS toxicity.

overall: **Recurrence-time delivery-enhancement pre-position; requires pre-screening at a SONOBIRD US site at the first-recurrence resection conversation.**

intervention_label: Front-line EGFRvIII / EGFR-amp CAR-T (MGH CARv3-TEAM-E NCT05660369 Arm 2 newly-diagnosed unmethylated; UCSF E-SYNC NCT06186401 Cohort 1; Penn dual-CAR family NCT07209241) — front-line use NOT recommended in this patient
expected_benefit: Choi 2024 NEJM CARv3-TEAM-E first-in-human (n=3, MGH): 3/3 near-complete radiographic regression within days of intraventricular infusion, no G≥3 AE in the lead cohort, no CRS ≥grade 2, no ICANS-defining events. Two of three progressed within 1-2 months, one was sustained at 150 days. Bagley 2024 NatMed Penn dual-target (n=6): 6/6 transient radiographic regression, 0% formal RANO objective response, 100% reversible ICANS-like neurotoxicity. Goff 2019 JIT (n=18): 0% ORR, 1 treatment-related death at >1e10 cells. O'Rourke 2017 STM (n=10): 1/10 SD at 18 months.
key_risks: Conservative-issued VETO on toxicity grounds for front-line use in this patient, contingent on (a) prior intratumoral hemorrhage and (b) absence of any phase 1 cohort that specifically addresses re-bleed risk under CRS / ICANS-mediated edema. Veto lifts to qualified-on-toxicity for recurrence-line consideration only IF E-SYNC Cohort 1 publishes a safety analysis that includes pre-bled patients with documented re-bleed surveillance.

Critic dissent on evidence quality: n=3 NEJM transient signal with 2/3 progressing inside two months is hypothesis-generating, not OS-validated; the cellular-therapy signal class is single-digit-n single-arm with transient signals at best.
Concensusite dissent on guideline fit: NCCN CNS v2.2026 does not endorse CAR-T at any line for GBM at any evidence category — no NCCN row, no EANO 2021 recommendation, no ESMO endorsement.

Advocate qualified critique on hemorrhage carry-forward: intraventricular CAR-T with the Bagley 2024 100% transient ICANS-like neurotox signal plus CRS-mediated cerebral edema on a pre-bled brain is heavier than a rank-2 placement (risktaker's original framing) would suggest.
Gated on EGFRvIII testing (currently unknown). E-SYNC Cohort 1 newly diagnosed front-line slot also requires unmethylated MGMT — two conditional gates compounded.
preference_alignment: Trial preference: nominally satisfied by risktaker's framing; foreclosed at front-line by the conservative veto. Efficacy lean 0.7: claimed by risktaker on the n=3 transient signal but the critic's evidence-quality framing reads this differently. Hemorrhage annotation: NOT respected at front-line per conservative veto.
guideline_status: Not in NCCN, EANO 2021, or ESMO — no front-line cellular-therapy endorsement at any evidence category for GBM.
rationale_summary: Surfaced as not_recommended at front-line per the universal-veto-with-documented-reasoning rule (PI contract hard rule #1). The conservative seat issued an explicit veto on toxicity grounds, citing prior intratumoral hemorrhage compounding the CRS / ICANS-mediated intracranial edema risk that none of the phase 1 readouts specifically address. The critic and consensusite dissented on evidence quality and guideline fit respectively; the advocate qualified the risktaker's rank-2 placement on the same hemorrhage carry-forward. Only the risktaker endorsed it at front-line, and even the risktaker's own writeup conceded the hemorrhage history is a real flag mitigated only by baseline imaging and an edema-management plan documented up front — which is acknowledgement, not mitigation. The synthesis carries the row visibly at the bottom of the ranked list so the reader sees what was considered and rejected, with the explicit lift-to-qualified-on-toxicity condition (E-SYNC Cohort 1 safety analysis including pre-bled patients) documented. At recurrence with EGFRvIII positivity and an explicit re-bleed-surveillance plan, the conversation re-opens.
open_questions: Whether E-SYNC Cohort 1 (UCSF) publishes a safety analysis that includes pre-bled patients with documented re-bleed surveillance — the conservative-veto lift-trigger.

EGFRvIII status (from the rank-1 NGS / RT-PCR bundle). Negative forecloses the entire cellular-therapy menu. Positive opens recurrence-time consideration at MGH (Curry / Maus, 617-724-6226), UCSF (Okada / Neuro-Onc New Patient Coord, 877-827-3222), or Penn (Bagley / Abramson Clinical Trials, 215-349-8245).
Whether intraventricular Ommaya reservoir placement is acceptable to the patient at the recurrence conversation; required for INCIPIENT / NCT05660369 enrollment.
likelihood_of_effect: Hypothesis-generating only — Choi 2024 n=3 transient signal with 2/3 progressing inside two months; class signal is single-digit-n single-arm with no OS validation.
toxicity_burden: High (Bagley 2024 100% transient ICANS-like neurotoxicity, Goff 2019 1 treatment-related death at >1e10 cells, hemorrhage-compounded edema risk in this patient)

counter_productive_moa.description: CRS / ICANS-mediated cerebral edema on a pre-bled brain is the conservative-flagged mechanism-level risk; no phase 1 cohort specifically addresses re-bleed risk under cellular-therapy inflammation.

overall: **Front-line CAR-T is not recommended in this patient — conservative veto stands on hemorrhage-compounded CRS / ICANS edema risk that the published phase 1 cohorts do not address. Recurrence-time conversation re-opens with EGFRvIII positivity and a hemorrhage-aware re-bleed surveillance plan.**
